items.content_html:
Firefox ignores the no-referrer-when-downgrade, origin-when-cross-origin and unsafe-url referrer policies for cross-site requests, and uses the default policy instead. This was added in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1720294 and enabled by default in Firefox 100 in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1761826.

The current data marks these values as removed in Firefox 92. This changes them to a partial implementation from Firefox 100, for the referrerpolicy attribute of <a>, <area>, <iframe>, <img>, <link> and <script>, the matching referrerPolicy properties, and the Referrer-Policy HTTP header.

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • 92-99 only ignored the values in Nightly and early Beta: the pref was @IS_EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER@ until https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1761826 set it to true.
  • Same-site requests still use the values, so they aren't removed.
  • Cross-site top-level navigations still use them outside private browsing (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1734328, also Firefox 100), which matters for <a>, <area> and the header (which also covers links followed from the page).

The same fix for svg.elements.a is in #31151.

Again, this seems reasonable to me from the bugs, but I'm hoping maybe you have tests for this?

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46466
items.title: Firefox relaxed referrer policies: partial from 100, not removed in 92

items.content_html:
FF161 adds support for the referrerpolicy attribute and referrerPolicy property on SVG <image>, <script> and <feImage> in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2079321

The collector added api.SVGScriptElement.referrerPolicy in #31035. This adds the remaining features:

  • api.SVGImageElement.referrerPolicy
  • api.SVGFEImageElement.referrerPolicy (non-standard: Filter Effects doesn't define referrerpolicy, see w3c/svgwg#1171)
  • svg.elements.image.referrerpolicy
  • svg.elements.script.referrerpolicy
  • svg.elements.feImage.referrerpolicy (non-standard)

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • Chrome: 113 for svg.elements.image.referrerpolicy only. Chrome's image loader reads referrerpolicy from whatever element it loads for, which includes SVG <image>, since chromium/chromium@4971c867d974 (refs/heads/main@{#1112277}). Chrome has no SVGImageElement.referrerPolicy property. The test results in w3c/svgwg#1171 show Chrome applies the attribute on <image> but not <script> or <feImage>, and Safari applies it on none of them.
  • Firefox ignores no-referrer-when-downgrade, origin-when-cross-origin and unsafe-url for cross-site requests from Firefox 100 (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1761826). This adds those subfeatures with Firefox as partial, and corrects the existing svg.elements.a data, which had them removed in 92.

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46466
items.title: FF161 SVG image, script and feImage referrerpolicy

items.content_html:
FF161 enables cross-document view transitions and render-blocking in Nightly in https://bugzil.la/2084340, by enabling the dom.viewTransitions.cross-document.enabled and dom.element.blocking.enabled prefs.

The collector run in #31035 (and #30918 for the @view-transition descriptors) set the delivered features to preview, except html.elements.link.rel.expect. Firefox implements rel=expect behind dom.element.blocking.enabled in https://bugzil.la/2053279 (HTMLLinkElement.cpp processes expect links, and relList.supports("expect") returns true, only when the pref is set).

This updates html.elements.link.rel.expect from false to preview.

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46469
items.title: FF161 Nightly supports link rel=expect

Summary

Samsung Browser 31 is out. Update the browser release list, and manually update api.SharedWorker as it only partially uses mirror.

Test results and supporting details

Release notes (or at least dates) are available for the Windows version on their website (https://developer.samsung.com/browser/release-note/windows-release-note.html), but not for the Android version.

The release date is based on the earliest APK uploaded to APKMirror (https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/samsung-electronics-co-ltd/samsung-internet-for-android/samsung-browser-31-0-0-64-release/). Based on those APKs, the 30 and 31 series overlapped for about a month, but it appears that some users of the release channel received version 31 on 2026-09-23.

Samsung Browser 31 appears to use Chromium 148, based on https://chromiumchecker.com/ and manual inspection of collector results.

Related issues

None

items.content_html:
The https://collector.openwebdocs.org/ project (v10.21.2) found new features shipping in Chromium 159 beta which was released yesterday. Currently, the collector covers about 90% of BCD, so the following list might not be exhaustive. Also, if a feature is in Canary/behind flags, it is not considered here. If a feature is missing, one reason can be that the IDL is not yet in a specification or in webref.

Chrome 159 stable releases on December 8, 2026. This PR needs to be merged before/with the BCD release on December 3, 2026.

With this PR, BCD will consider the following features as shipping in Chromium 159:

items.content_html:
FF161 enables support for ClipboardItem custom formats (types prefixed with web ) by default on desktop and Android in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2053725

This updates api.ClipboardItem.type_web from preview to 161, and adds notes for the Firefox-specific read restrictions (the spec doesn't restrict reads by origin):

  • Custom formats can only be read if the clipboard contains same-origin content. Firefox treats data from other applications as cross-origin. https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2086505
  • Extensions with clipboardRead can read custom formats from any origin. https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2087427

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46463
items.title: FF161 ClipboardItem web custom formats enabled by default

items.content_html:
FF161 adds support for the setParameterOptions argument of RTCRtpSender.setParameters(), and its encodingOptions property (an array of objects with a keyFrame property), in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2057265

This adds api.RTCRtpSender.setParameters.setParameterOptions_encodingOptions_parameter. keyFrame is the only member of each encodingOptions item, so it doesn't get its own subfeature.

  • Chrome: 122. Added in chromium/chromium@b53076683b (refs/heads/main@{#1249577}), and https://chromestatus.com/feature/5161082937409536 says 122.
  • Safari: false. WebKit's RTCRtpSender.idl still declares only setParameters(RTCRtpSendParameters parameters).

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46464
items.title: FF161 RTCRtpSender.setParameters() setParameterOptions.encodingOptions

Summary

Adds the password_option subfeature under api.CredentialsContainer.create to reflect that passing a password option is not supported in Safari or Firefox.

Test results and supporting details

  • Ran npm run format, npm run lint, and the repository unit test suite locally with all checks passing.
  • Safari unsupported status: https://webkit.org/b/252908
  • Firefox unsupported status: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1156047
  • Note: Chrome 60 is inferred from CredentialsContainer.create() (Chrome 60) and PasswordCredential (Chrome 51) support rather than tested on a live Chrome 60 binary.

Related issues

Fixes #7941
